Definition: the little man of the eye; the pupil or ball; hence, the middle (of night)
BiblicalUsage: The apple of the eye is the pupil, the tenderest part, and God uses it for his people. In Deuteronomy 32:10 he keeps Jacob as the apple of his eye, in Psalms 17:8 David prays, keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings, and in Proverbs 7:2 the father says, keep my law as the apple of thine eye.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the picture is the tenderest in the Bible: God guards his people the way an eye guards its pupil. He is quick to close and quick to keep.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
